title: NY State Assembly · District 32
area: Southeast Queens, including Jamaica, South Jamaica, Rochdale Village, St. Albans, Locust Manor, and parts of Richmond Hill and South Ozone Park

context.text: Longtime incumbent Vivian Cook (in office since 1991) is not seeking re-election, leaving District 32 an open seat.

Nathaniel Hezekiah III won a five-way June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote over Latoya LeGrand, Mohammed Molla, Tunisia Morrison, and Queen Johnson. LeGrand had also won the Working Families Party primary but withdrew from that general-election line.

candidates.name: Nathaniel Hezekiah III
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote in a five-candidate field

summary.text: Nathaniel Hezekiah III is a South Jamaica, Queens native who, according to his campaign website, has spent nearly two decades in the office of U.S. Representative Gregory Meeks, rising to Deputy Chief of Staff. He won a five-way Democratic primary on June 23, 2026 for the open Assembly District 32 seat, and says he is running to continue serving the community that raised him.

background.text: Hezekiah says he was born and raised in South Jamaica, Queens. According to his campaign website, his family moved to Richmond, Virginia, in the 1980s, and his mother brought the children back to Southeast Queens after his father was killed by gun violence.
He attended P.S. 160 and New Preparatory Middle School, then studied in the law program at Benjamin N. Cardozo High School, according to his campaign website.
He attended St. John's University before transferring to Pennsylvania State University, where his campaign website says he earned two bachelor's degrees, in business and finance.

He began his career with Amalgamated Transit Union Local 1056, then joined the staff of Congressman Gregory Meeks, working up to Deputy Chief of Staff, according to his campaign website. The Queens Chronicle reported in early 2026 that he had previously served as Meeks’ project manager and community liaison.

His campaign website describes constituent-service work in Meeks’ office, including help with Social Security, Medicare, immigration and veterans benefits, and says he helped recover more than $13 million owed to Rochdale Village residents and directed more than $100,000 in scholarship funding for local students.

He declared his candidacy for Assembly District 32 after Assemblymember Vivian Cook announced she would not seek re-election after 35 years in office. The Queens County Democratic Party backed him, and Meeks supported his candidacy.
Hezekiah won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote over Latoya LeGrand, Mohammed Molla, Tunisia Morrison and Queen Johnson.

priorities.text: Hezekiah's campaign slogan frames his candidacy around a record of service: "When It Mattered. Nathaniel was there."
priorities.quote: When It Mattered. Nathaniel was there.

priorities.text: He cites accomplishments including directing more than $100,000 in scholarship funding for local students, helping recover more than $13 million owed to the Rochdale Village community, and supporting minority- and women-owned business participation in the JFK Airport redevelopment.

His platform lists housing and homeownership assistance, protecting Mitchell-Lama communities, economic development, transportation equity, a "cradle-to-career" education pipeline, protecting the social safety net, and public safety as priorities.
He states his overall commitment is "strengthening opportunity, protecting affordability, and making sure government works for the people it serves."
priorities.quote: Nathaniel is committed to strengthening opportunity, protecting affordability, and making sure government works for the people it serves.

positions.summary: Campaigns on expanding paths to homeownership and homeownership assistance for district residents.
Lists protecting Mitchell-Lama affordable-housing communities as a campaign priority.

summary.text: Paul Nichols is on the November ballot for Assembly District 32 on The Answer Party line. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and no campaign website or public policy statements were found.
